description: Reads what this project's ads did; it spends nothing. Without id: Marsell's own count per ad and campaign over the days: visits, accounts opened, paid subscriptions and their money (refunds off) against spend, the cost of each result, every ad visit and result with its source; beside it the network's claim, never added to Marsell's count (counting.on false: not counted here yet, and why). Then records: every real ad's record, newest first: what it showed, what it was bought for (boughtFor), its days, the most approved, its spend in the ad account's currency, what the network counted (a number it did not report is left out, never 0), the costs that follow, and comparedWith: earlier ended ads on the same network, bought for the same thing, counted the same way, in the same currency. Rehearsal ads are left out and counted. With id: that one ad whole, every day's numbers, approvals, settings sent, compared ads by id. A record is measurement; one ad is one observation. Every ad on Sell is place_open sell.

days.description: The span, in days ending today, 1 to 365: Marsell's count over it, and only the records of ads that ran in it. Left out: 90 days of the count, and every record.

id.description: One ad's id, as records gives it: that ad whole instead of the lists. "" or left out for the lists.

only.description: Only the records with this network (meta, google, linkedin, tiktok, pinterest, x, reddit, openai), this kind (boost: a boosted post; campaign: the owner's own Meta campaign; google_campaign; test_ad: one of a test's two ads) or this state (starting, in_review, running, paused, rejected, ended, failed); "" or left out for every record.

project.description: The project's id or exact name. Optional when the account has one project.

title: Read what ads brought
